Let me create a final report with all the key findings: ## Component Architecture Summary: Rankora Recruiter Job View Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here's the exact component architecture for how recruiters view jobs and candidates: ### 1. **Navigation & View Hierarchy** **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/pages/Index.tsx` (lines 1-407) Navigation flow: - **Dashboard** (view="dashboard") → Shows recent jobs + stats - **My Jobs** (view="my-jobs") → Full job listing + management - **Job Detail** (view="job-detail") → Main recruiter workspace - **New Job** (view="new-job") → Job creation mode When a job is selected via `loadJobData(jobId)`, the view switches to "job-detail" and fetches: - Resume data from `resumes` table (id, filename, file_path, candidate_name, created_at, parsed_json) - Result/scoring data from `results` table (overall_score, missing_skills, category_scores, confidence, strengths, gaps, explanation, matched_must_haves, missing_must_haves, scoring_version) ### 2. **JobDetailView Component Structure** **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/JobDetailView.tsx` (1650 lines) **Key Props**: ```typescript interface JobDetailViewProps { selectedJobId: string | null; selectedJob: PastJob | null; results: Result[]; setResults: (results: Result[] | ((prev: Result[]) => Result[])) => void; existingResumes: ExistingResume[]; setExistingResumes: (resumes: ExistingResume[] | ((prev: ExistingResume[]) => ExistingResume[])) => void; onJobCreated: (job: PastJob) => void; onAuthRequired: () => void; isAuthenticated?: boolean; pastJobs?: PastJob[]; onJobUpdated?: (jobId: string, updates: Partial) => void; onBack?: () => void; } ``` **State Management** (lines 76-101): - `activeTab: "resumes" | "applications"` (line 101) — **Already has tab system!** - `stageFilter: HiringStage | null` — Filter candidates by hiring stage - `showArchived: boolean` — Toggle archived candidate visibility - `selectedCandidateId: string | null` — Currently selected candidate for detail sheet - `dismissedResumes: Set` — Archived candidates - Various ranking/upload states **Hiring Stage Tracker Integration** (lines 116-130): - Uses `useStages(selectedJobId)` hook to fetch stage data - Uses `useUpdateStage()` to update candidate stages - Maps candidates to hiring stages: applied → screened → interview → offer → hired/rejected **Candidates Data Processing** (lines 140-151): ```typescript const resultResumeIds = new Set(results.map((r) => r.resume_id)); const pendingResumes: Result[] = existingResumes .filter((r) => !resultResumeIds.has(r.id)) .map((r) => ({...r, pending: true})); const allResults = [...results, ...pendingResumes]; ``` **Filtering Logic** (lines 782-788): ```typescript const nonArchivedResults = allResults.filter((r) => !dismissedResumes.has(r.resume_id)); const visibleResults = nonArchivedResults.filter((r) => { if (!stageFilter) return true; const candidateStage = stageMap.get(r.resume_id)?.stage ?? Timestamp display - Empty state with "No applications yet" message - Status count badges in header - Responsive table design ### 5. **Individual Candidate Detail Sheet** **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` (190 lines) Used by CandidateRow (right panel detail view): **Key Sections** (in order): 1. **Header** — Dark hero with candidate name, location, email, match score, badges 2. **Action buttons** — Phone, Email, Download resume, Archive 3. **Stage Tracker** — Visual hiring pipeline 4. **JD Alignment Panel** — How well candidate fits the job 5. **Summary** — AI's assessment of candidate 6. **Strengths & Gaps** — Quick signals 7. **Skills Detail** — Technical breakdown 8. **Experience & Education** — Two-column layout 9. **Interview Prep** — AI-generated interview questions **Integration with JobDetailView**: ```typescript setSelectedCandidateId(null)} jobId={selectedJobId} jobTitle={selectedJob?.title} formatCandidateName={formatCandidateName} onDownload={handleDownload} onDismiss={handleDismissCandidate} currentStage={stageMap.get(selectedCandidateId)?.stage} stageUpdatedAt={stageMap.get(selectedCandidateId)?.updated_at} onStageChange={handleStageChange} /> ``` ### 6. **Resumes Tab UI Structure** **Lines 1205-1630**: Main resume ranking interface **Sections**: 1. **JD Card** (left column, lines 874-983): - Progress bar with detailed messaging - Error handling (credits, rate limits, generic errors) - Stuck job detection with retry button 5. **Pending Resumes Banner** (lines 1276-1295): - Prompts recruiter to rank new resumes - Shows count of pending candidates 6. **Results Table** (lines 1297-1630): - Sticky header with stage filter buttons + archive toggle - Select all / deselect all for bulk operations - Candidate rows (rendered via CandidateRow component) - Actions: bulk delete, export to CSV - Row interaction: click to open CandidateDetailSheet - Stage badges on candidates - Duplicate detection badges - Sorting by score (descending) ### 7. **Candidate Row Component** **File**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/CandidateRow.tsx` (210 lines) **Displays per candidate**: - Checkbox for bulk selection - Rank # (1, 2, 3...) - Candidate name + location + duplicate badge + stage badge - Score % with progress bar - Strength label (Strong/Good/Weak) + Quick badge + Confidence % - Quick action buttons: Copy phone, Email, Download resume, Archive **Example row data flow**: 1. User clicks CandidateRow → opens CandidateDetailSheet in right panel 2. User clicks "Archive" → candidate moved to dismissedResumes 3. User clicks stage badge on row → calls handleStageChange → updates DB + UI 4. User clicks "Email" button → opens EmailOutreachDialog ### 8. **Data Integration Points** **From Index.tsx**: - `pastJobs` — list of all jobs - `results` — ranked candidates for selected job - `existingResumes` — uploaded resumes (pending + ranked) - `selectedJob` — current job details **Database Tables**: - `jobs` (id, user_id, title, job_description, status, created_at, jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json, inbox_email) - `resumes` (id, job_id, filename, file_path, candidate_name, created_at, parsed_json) - `results` (id, resume_id, overall_score, missing_skills, summary, interview_questions, hard_fit, category_scores_json, confidence, strengths_json, gaps_json, explanation_json, matched_must_haves, missing_must_haves, scoring_version) - `hiring_stages` (resume_id, job_id, stage, updated_at) - `applications` (id, job_id, name, email, phone, linkedin_url, resume_path, resume_filename, status, created_at) ### 9. **Architecture Diagram** ``` Index.tsx (Dashboard/MyJobs/JobDetail Navigation) ↓ JobDetailView.tsx ├─ [Resumes Tab] (activeTab === "resumes") │ ├─ JD Card (left) │ ├─ Upload + Inbox Card (right) │ ├─ Results Table │ │ └─ CandidateRow × N (clickable) │ │ ├─ CandidateDetailSheet (opens in right panel) │ │ │ ├─ CandidateSummary │ │ │ ├─ SkillsDetailPanel │ │ │ ├─ ExperiencePanel │ │ │ ├─ EducationPanel │ │ │ ├─ JDAlignedPanel │ │ │ ├─ StrengthsGapsPanel │ │ │ ├─ InterviewQuestionsPanel │ │ │ └─ StageTracker │ │ └─ EmailOutreachDialog │ └─ HiringStageFilter (applied/screened/interview/offer/hired/rejected) │ └─ [Applications Tab] (activeTab === "applications") └─ ApplicationsTab.tsx └─ Applications Table └─ Application Row × N ├─ Status dropdown (pending/reviewed/shortlisted/rejected) ├─ Resume download └─ LinkedIn link ``` ### Summary for Integration **Where to add/enhance Applications view**: 1. ✅ Tab system already exists at lines 1150-1186 2. ✅ ApplicationsTab component already mounted at line 1185 3. ✅ Applications database table with candidate data 4. **Could enhance**: - Add individual application detail sheet (similar to CandidateDetailSheet) - Link applications to ranked candidates in Resumes tab - Add application-to-candidate matching/reconciliation - Add workflow status management (under review, scheduling interview, etc.) - Add bulk email templates for applications The architecture is **tab-based**: Recruiters toggle between Resumes (ranking/screening) and Applications (intake management) views within the same job context.
